fields.why: The notice reports quantities and a comparison (rate fell 39%, 9.7 to 5.9 per 100,000; proportion 50% to 38%) cited from earlier reports to frame a call to action, which the brief names as 'limited'; 'none' requires no such quantities.
Follows from data_focus limited: death rates per 100,000 and the alcohol-related proportion of traffic fatalities are stated.
1998 counts are summaries and 1988 vs 1998 values are compared with a computed percent decrease.
The primary contrast is two years, 1988 vs 1998; the 5.5 per 100,000 objective is stated but not explicitly contrasted.
'decreased 39%' is a percent change, i.e. a relative scale.
The cited figures are a 1988-1998 trend and two-point comparison; under the brief two time points compared count as before/after.

brief_issues: Awareness-month announcements that cite a few trend figures sit on the none/limited boundary; the brief could state explicitly that any cited outcome quantity makes an announcement 'limited'.
